To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the real gas, restricted valve model is necessary to accurately predict the performance of a swashplate electric refrigeration compressor as a function of operating rpm.
the real-gas, minor-loss discharge-coeffient model is the most accurate model for predicting the discharge temperature of an electric swash-plate compressor.

the real-gas, real-valve model predicts the compressor performance better than the ideal-gas, real valve model, and the real-gas ideal-valve model is not a good approximation for a swashplate refrigerant compressor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a real-gas compressor model for a swashplate-type refrigeration compressor.
the modeling and simulation of the thermodynamic performance of a real gas swashplate refrigerating compressor.
developing a model that is capable of predicting the performance of a real-gas compressor with real-gas properties, and that includes the effect of valve flow restrictions on compressor performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

real-gas properties are important for the prediction of compressor performance, especially for the discharge temperature, while minor-loss discharge coefficients are important in predicting the refrigerant mass flow and the volumetric efficiency.
the real-gas, real-valve model is the most reliable for the simulation of a swashplate compressor.
the ideal-gas model is not suitable for modeling a swashplate refrigerant compressor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of real-gas properties is essential for predicting the performance of an electric swash-plate refrigeration compressor, while the minor-loss valve model is sufficient to predict the performance of a swashplate compressor with a mechanical drive.
a real-gas, minor-loss discharge-coefficients valve model can predict swashplate refrigerant compressor performance with a reasonable level of accuracy.
the ideal-gas, restricted-discharge valve model is a reasonable approximation for the performance of a swashplate compressor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the real-gas, minor-loss discharge-coefficients approach is the best way to model the performance of an electric swash-plate refrigeration compressor.
the use of real-gas properties in the compressor model can improve the prediction of compressor performance as a function of operating conditions.
a model for the real gas behavior of the refrigerant in the compressor is necessary to accurately predict performance as a function of speed and to understand how the compressor operates.
